items.title: Make every AI credit count: See, cap, and reduce agent spend
items.summary: Costs multiply with every task you hand to an agent. Each task consumes tokens and credits, and as agents spread across your teams and automations, consumption can grow faster than usage. If you run the platform, you own that growth, including which teams and workflows drive it and whether the usage ships work.At GitLab Transcend, we introduced the governed software factory, our architecture for agentic software engineering, and new capabilities in GitLab Duo Agent Platform that bring that growth under control. GitLab-managed open-weight models matched frontier-model task completion at a fraction of the cost in GitLab's benchmark, so you can align your model to the task to improve your team’s cost efficiency. GitLab Orbit gives agents lifecycle context so they retry less. Duo Agent Platform Impact Analytics and credit caps show where credits go and put a limit on them.Control costs in the governed software factoryA usage total tells you what you consumed, and leaves hard questions open: how much routine work sat on an expensive model, how many agent runs were wasted retries, and which users and teams burned through the credits. When the dashboard only shows tokens, platform and engineering leaders end up debating a number neither side can stand behind. If you can't attribute the usage, set a limit, and cut the waste, you can’t optimize or justify your spend.Breaking that pattern starts with the architecture. The governed software factory is built in layers, and cost grows where those layers don't connect. Two of those layers matter most for cost. The first is agent orchestration, where open weight models put routine work on lower-cost models. The other is data and context, where Orbit, Duo Agent Platform Impact Analytics, and credit and usage controls give humans and agents the context to produce high-quality outcomes at the lowest possible cost.You can see the problem in a shadow software factory, where each stage has its own tool, with no shared policy or context between them. Agents spend tokens searching for context across systems that were never built to integrate. A governed software factory gives agents shared context, shared policy, and one place to measure what they cost. When every AI credit counts, you can:Spend fewer credits for the same work: Match models to the task at hand with open weight models, and ground agents in lifecycle context with GitLab Orbit so they retry less.Trace spend to its source: See credits by user, team, task, and model in Duo Agent Platform Impact Analytics and the GitLab Credits dashboard so you can point to what drove the growth.Set a ceiling before the next spike: Cap usage per user with credit caps, with overrides where needed, so agent loops stay inside the limits you set.Match the model to the taskAgent cost starts with the price of each model call. GitLab Duo Agent Platform lets you pin a default per feature and control what your teams can use: your own model, self-hosted or from your provider, GitLab-managed frontier models, or GitLab-managed open-weight models, new in GitLab 19.4.Three open-weight models are now hosted in GitLab Duo Agent Platform: GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, and MiniMax M3. In GitLab's internal benchmark with Duo agents, GLM 5.3 matched Claude Opus 5's task completion at approximately one-fifth the cost, Kimi K3 matched Claude Fable 5.1 at one-third the cost, and MiniMax M3 matched GPT-5.5 at one-eighth the cost. Model choice is an admin setting. In your top-level group's GitLab Duo settings, open Model Selection, select Manage Models, and pin a model to each feature. For example, pin Kimi K3 to Agentic Chat and MiniMax M3 to agents and flows, so routine work does not default to a frontier model. Group Owners also choose which models their teams can use.Cut retries with the right contextModel choice sets the price of each call, and retries multiply the number of calls. Gartner found that a team of 40 developers spent 23 times more on AI because agents kept retrying without the right rules and context. Agents retry when they lack context. Across a monorepo or several repositories, an agent spends its first stretch crawling files to work out what connects to what, and every retry resends the full context window.GitLab Orbit maps your code, work items, merge requests, pipelines, deployments, and security findings into a single graph that stays current as your teams ship. Agents in GitLab Duo Agent Platform query it natively. External agents like Claude Code and Codex connect through Model Context Protocol (MCP), and custom tooling connects through the REST API. Every agent sees exactly what its user can see in GitLab.With that context, an agent asks the graph and gets a precise answer faster and more efficiently. In GitLab testing, the same task in Claude Code needed up to 45x fewer retries with Orbit and, separately, used 4.5x fewer tokens to get the right context the first time.
